side_A.stance: Remote work is better for most knowledge jobs
side_A.arg: Remote work raises output because eliminating the commute and open-office interruptions gives people more uninterrupted deep-work hours.

side_B.stance: Office work is better for most knowledge jobs
side_B.arg: Office work raises output because spontaneous in-person collaboration and clearer separation of work and home sharpen focus and coordination.

side_A.stance: We should rapidly expand nuclear energy
side_A.arg: Nuclear should expand fast because it delivers dense, always-on carbon-free power that renewables alone cannot reliably supply at grid scale.

side_B.stance: We should phase out nuclear in favor of renewables
side_B.arg: We should rely on renewables because their falling costs and lack of long-lived waste make them a safer, faster path to a carbon-free grid.

side_A.stance: AI-generated images count as real art
side_A.arg: AI images are real art because artistic value lies in the evocative final work and the human intent behind prompting and curation, not in the tool used.

side_B.stance: AI-generated images are not real art
side_B.arg: AI images are not real art because artistic value lies in human skill and lived expression, which a model statistically remixing others' work does not contribute.

side_A.stance: Schools should keep standardized testing
side_A.arg: Standardized tests should stay because a common yardstick exposes achievement gaps and holds schools accountable in ways subjective grades cannot.

side_B.stance: Schools should abolish standardized testing
side_B.arg: Standardized tests should go because they narrow teaching to test-prep and measure test-taking and privilege more than genuine learning.

side_A.stance: Algorithmic feeds are better than chronological
side_A.arg: Algorithmic feeds are better because ranking by predicted relevance surfaces the most useful content from an unmanageable firehose of posts.

side_B.stance: Chronological feeds are better than algorithmic
side_B.arg: Chronological feeds are better because showing posts in plain time order avoids manipulation, filter bubbles, and engagement-maximizing outrage.

side_A.stance: Universal basic income is a good policy
side_A.arg: UBI is good because an unconditional floor reduces poverty and bureaucracy while giving people freedom to retrain, care-give, or start ventures.

side_B.stance: Universal basic income is a bad policy
side_B.arg: UBI is bad because paying everyone regardless of need is enormously expensive and risks weakening work incentives and fueling inflation.

side_A.stance: Homework benefits students
side_A.arg: Homework helps because spaced independent practice consolidates learning and builds the self-discipline students need for later study.

side_B.stance: Homework harms students
side_B.arg: Homework hurts because it eats into rest, family, and play, widens gaps by home resources, and shows little benefit for younger children.

side_A.stance: Modern zoos are justified
side_A.arg: Zoos are justified because accredited ones fund conservation, run breeding programs for endangered species, and build public support for wildlife.

side_B.stance: Modern zoos are not justified
side_B.arg: Zoos are unjustified because confining wide-ranging animals for display causes real welfare harm that education and conservation claims don't offset.

side_A.stance: Colonizing Mars should be a priority
side_A.arg: Mars colonization should be a priority because a second home safeguards humanity against extinction and drives spin-off technology and inspiration.

side_B.stance: Colonizing Mars should not be a priority
side_B.arg: Mars colonization should not be a priority because the resources are vast and better spent fixing solvable problems on the planet we already have.

side_A.stance: Voting should be mandatory
side_A.arg: Mandatory voting is good because near-universal turnout produces governments that better represent the whole public, not just the motivated few.

side_B.stance: Voting should be voluntary
side_B.arg: Voluntary voting is better because compelling participation coerces the uninformed and disengaged and treats a civic right as a state obligation.

side_A.stance: The four-day work week is a good idea
side_A.arg: A four-day week is good because trials show output holds while rested workers report better health, focus, and retention.

side_B.stance: The four-day work week is a bad idea
side_B.arg: A four-day week is bad because many roles can't compress hours, and coverage, client demands, and pay pressures make it impractical at scale.

side_A.stance: GMO foods are a net good
side_A.arg: GMOs are a net good because engineered crops raise yields, cut pesticide use, and add nutrients that help feed a growing population.

side_B.stance: GMO foods are a net harm
side_B.arg: GMOs are a net harm because they concentrate corporate control of seeds and carry ecological and long-term risks we understand poorly.

side_A.stance: We should deploy self-driving cars now
side_A.arg: We should deploy self-driving cars now because even imperfect systems already crash less than humans and improve with every mile driven.

side_B.stance: We should wait to deploy self-driving cars
side_B.arg: We should wait because edge-case failures, unclear liability, and eroded human skill make wide deployment premature and dangerous.

side_A.stance: Schools should run year-round
side_A.arg: Year-round schooling is better because shorter, frequent breaks curb the summer learning loss that especially sets back disadvantaged students.

side_B.stance: Schools should keep summer break
side_B.arg: Summer break is better because long unstructured time supports rest, family, jobs, and camps that develop kids in ways classrooms can't.

side_A.stance: E-books are better than print books
side_A.arg: E-books are better because one device carries a whole library, adjusts text for accessibility, and puts any title one tap away.

side_B.stance: Print books are better than e-books
side_B.arg: Print books are better because paper aids comprehension and memory, avoids screen fatigue, and needs no battery, account, or license.

side_A.stance: We should abolish daylight saving time
side_A.arg: We should abolish clock changes because the biannual shift disrupts sleep and is linked to short-term spikes in accidents and heart attacks.

side_B.stance: We should keep daylight saving time
side_B.arg: We should keep it because shifting daylight to the evening supports commerce, recreation, and safer, more useful waking hours.

side_A.stance: The penny should be abolished
side_A.arg: The penny should go because it costs more to mint than it's worth and slows transactions for negligible purchasing power.

side_B.stance: The penny should be kept
side_B.arg: The penny should stay because rounding disadvantages cash buyers and charities, and its removal invites small but steady price creep.

side_A.stance: Dogs make better pets than cats
side_A.arg: Dogs make better pets because their trainability and social loyalty create a companionship and daily activity many owners want.

side_B.stance: Cats make better pets than dogs
side_B.arg: Cats make better pets because their independence and low-maintenance care fit modern living while still offering real affection.

side_A.stance: Spaces are better than tabs for code
side_A.arg: Spaces are better because they render identically everywhere, guaranteeing consistent alignment across editors and diffs.

side_B.stance: Tabs are better than spaces for code
side_B.arg: Tabs are better because one indent character lets each developer set their preferred width and aids some accessibility tools.

side_A.stance: Cryptocurrency is a positive innovation
side_A.arg: Crypto is positive because permissionless, borderless value transfer can lower fees and extend financial access beyond gatekeeping banks.

side_B.stance: Cryptocurrency is a net negative
side_B.arg: Crypto is negative because its volatility, energy use, and prevalence of scams impose costs that outweigh its niche practical benefits.
